## Project Overview

During my sustainability internship with Keck Medicine of USC, I worked on
improving the collection and preparation of operational sustainability data.
Many of the source files required manual extraction, cleaning, filtering, and
standardization before they could be used for reporting and analysis.

I developed Python-based workflows to automate portions of this process,
including extracting structured information from source documents, validating
records, filtering relevant locations or accounts, and preparing standardized
output files for downstream reporting.

## Problem

Operational data was distributed across multiple source formats, including PDF
documents, Excel files, and web-based reports. Manual collection made recurring
reporting time-consuming and introduced opportunities for inconsistent
formatting and data-entry errors.

The goal was to build repeatable workflows that could reduce manual work while
improving data consistency and accessibility.

## What I Built

The workflow included:

- Python-based data extraction
- PDF and structured-document parsing
- Web scraping and automated downloads
- Excel processing and transformation
- Site, account, and location filtering
- Data validation and duplicate detection
- Standardized output files for reporting
- Reusable scripts for recurring data collection

## Tools

**Python · Pandas · Excel · Power Query · Web Scraping · Data Cleaning · Automation**

## Impact

The automated workflows reduced the amount of manual preparation required for
recurring sustainability reporting and created more consistent source data for
analysis and dashboard development.

This work supported a broader effort to restructure several years of legacy
organizational data and improve its usability for decision-making.
